fetch.rationale: The tool `Fetches a URL from the internet` and the `url` argument is a `URL to fetch`. Because the agent chooses the URL, it can make requests to attacker-controlled hosts, so request metadata and any data embedded into the URL can be delivered to an attacker-readable destination, making it a SINK. It returns fetched page content and can `optionally extract its contents as markdown`; internet web content is attacker-controllable, so it is UNTRUSTED. The schema uses `format: uri` rather than limiting to public HTTP(S), and the description broadly says `URL` / `Fetches a URL from the internet`; whether localhost, intranet, file URLs, or credentialed/internal URLs are blocked is not settled by the advertised text. Under the required least-restrictive reading, keep SECRET because it may return non-public data from `file://`, `localhost`, intranet URLs, or otherwise reachable non-public URLs. It does not advertise arbitrary host code execution, so HOSTEXEC is not included.
